facts.fact_text: On 2 April 2011 the first applicant attended an unauthorised opposition demonstration held at Fountains Square in Baku.
On 2 April 2011 the second applicant attended an unauthorised opposition demonstration held at Fountains Square in Baku.
The demonstration held at Fountains Square on 2 April 2011 was intended to be peaceful.
The demonstration held at Fountains Square on 2 April 2011 was conducted in a peaceful manner.
The participants of the demonstration held at Fountains Square on 2 April 2011 were demanding free and fair elections.
The participants of the demonstration held at Fountains Square on 2 April 2011 were demanding democratic reforms.
The participants of the demonstration held at Fountains Square on 2 April 2011 were demanding freedom of assembly.
The participants of the demonstration held at Fountains Square on 2 April 2011 were demanding the release of people arrested during some previous demonstrations.
Upon arriving at Fountains Square at around 3 p.m. on 2 April 2011, the first applicant was arrested by police officers.
The Nasimi District Court convicted the first applicant under Article 310.1 (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer) of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The Nasimi District Court sentenced the first applicant to eight days' administrative detention.

At around 2 p.m. on 2 April 2011, while the second applicant was chanting during the demonstration at Fountains Square, four police officers approached him and twisted his arms behind his back in order to put him in a police car.
After the second applicant regained consciousness, the officers dragged him to a police car and took him to the Sabail district police office.
The second applicant was reprimanded for participating in a public assembly under Article 298 (violation of the rules on holding public assemblies) of the Code of Administrative Offences.

The Nasimi District Court sentenced the first applicant to eight days' administrative detention.

The Nasimi District Court relied on the testimony of police officer A.E., who testified that the first applicant had been attempting to hold an unauthorised demonstration and had continued his actions, disobeying a request to stop participating in the unlawful demonstration.

The first applicant was allegedly beaten by S.N., who was the Deputy Head of the Nasimi district police office.
The first applicant was allegedly beaten by a police officer called J.A.
The first applicant was allegedly beaten by a person wearing plain clothes whom the first applicant did not know.
According to the first applicant, S.N. (Deputy Head of the Nasimi district police office) kicked the first applicant in his abdominal area.
According to the first applicant, S.N. (Deputy Head of the Nasimi district police office) punched the first applicant.
According to the first applicant, after S.N. (Deputy Head of the Nasimi district police office) kicked him in his testicles, the first applicant lost consciousness owing to the severe pain.
According to a forensic report dated 15 April 2011, there was an abrasion on the first applicant's left calf caused by a blunt object.
According to the forensic report dated 15 April 2011, the abrasion on the first applicant's left calf could have been inflicted on 2 April 2011.
By a decision of 28 April 2011, the Nasimi district prosecutor's office refused to open a criminal case regarding the first applicant's alleged ill-treatment.

The Nasimi district prosecutor's office refused to open a criminal case on the grounds that the first applicant's beating by S.N. (Deputy Head of the Nasimi district police office) had not been proved.
On 21 June 2011 the Nasimi District Court held that the Nasimi district prosecutor's office's decision of 28 April 2011 to refuse to open a criminal case had been lawful.
By a judgment of 14 July 2011, the Baku Court of Appeal upheld the Nasimi District Court's decision of 21 June 2011.

S.N. (Deputy Head of the Nasimi district police office) insulted the second applicant and twisted his arm even more, saying to the police officers, "You should not twist [his arms], but break them, like this".
Under S.N.'s orders, police officers beat the second applicant with truncheons.
The second applicant lost consciousness and lay on the ground for several minutes after being beaten with truncheons.
A forensic report dated 4 April 2011 stated that the second applicant had a bruise on his left arm.
The forensic report dated 4 April 2011 stated that the bruise on the second applicant's left arm could have been caused on 2 April 2011.
According to the second applicant's medical records of 5 April 2011, issued by the medical centre, the second applicant had contusion of the soft tissues of his left upper arm and thorax.
According to the second applicant's medical records of 5 April 2011, the second applicant had thoracic bruising.
According to the second applicant's medical records of 5 April 2011, the second applicant had haemarthrosis of his right elbow joint.
By a decision of 5 May 2011, the Sabail district prosecutor's office refused to open a criminal case regarding the second applicant's alleged ill-treatment.
The Sabail district prosecutor's office found that there was no evidence that the second applicant had been beaten by police during his arrest.
On 13 June 2011 the Nasimi District Court dismissed the second applicant's complaint, finding the investigator's decision to refuse to open a criminal case lawful.
On 24 June 2011 the Baku Court of Appeal upheld the Nasimi District Court's decision of 13 June 2011 as lawful.
The relevant domestic law concerning the prohibition of ill-treatment is summarised in the case of Mustafa Hajili v. Azerbaijan (no. 42119/12, paragraphs 26-28, 24 November 2016).
